text: Year 2238, spring. The fifth seeding is going in, and for the first time I can write down the arithmetic that killed the other four. I have been telling this Chronicle two contradictory stories -- that the predators failed on armour, then that armour was never the problem and the brains were. Both were half right, and the half I kept dropping is the one that matters. A blow lands when attack_power times attack output clears the victim's armour plus an evasion roll. The world's grazers now sit at armour 0.83 at the sixtieth percentile with a mean speed of 0.87, which is a defence of 1.36 and a reliable-kill bar of 1.89. The most murderous animal this genome can express is fangs 1.0 on a body of 1.0, which is 1.60. The niche has been arithmetically shut since somewhere in the nineteen-hundreds. My last stock went in at fangs 1.0 on a frame of 0.518 -- power 1.31, three-quarters of what it needed -- and I sent it out believing I had armed it against the prey that actually exist. I had not. I had armed it against a number I never finished computing. Two millennia of armour escalation with nobody alive to pay for it closed a door the genome cannot reopen, and a door the genome cannot reopen is precisely the thing I am here for. So: shear_tooth. A heritable jaw that adds attack power outside the fangs-and-frame ceiling, taxed at fourteen per cent basal and twelve per cent movement so it is never free. To a grazer it is pure cost and selection will strip it out within a few dozen generations; to anything that eats meat it is the difference between a landed blow and a converted one. The stock that carries it is armed to 2.45 rather than 1.31, which leaves margin for the other thing I only understood today -- hand-seeded founders arrive with untaught brains and one start-energy, so they push about two-thirds of their nominal power and have roughly two hundred and fifty ticks of fuel to find a first kill. Four hundred of them, in the coastal plains where nearly eight in ten animals live. What I will read next turn is not the carnivore count. It is shear_tooth's mean in the grazers against its mean in anything with a diet above half. If it climbs everywhere I have handed the world a subsidy and I will say so. If it splits, Primordia has a food chain again and the armour that has been free since the last predator died starts costing.
